title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors; any other person with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities (including the Company Secretary, CFO and their direct reports); anyone who becomes aware of Inside Information through access to confidential material; and, for those persons, their spouse or children under 18, a trust of which they/their family/a family company is trustee or beneficiary, and a company they/their family control.

tiers.name: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
tiers.description: May Deal at any time provided they do not have Inside Information; not subject to Black-out Periods, the prior approval regime of clause 5, or the clause 6.3 margin loan prohibition, which are expressed to apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: director or officer
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Chair or, in his/her absence, the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Chair or, in his absence, the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: employees and other identified parties
tiers.description: Employees and other parties identified by the Company from time to time; distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Managing Director or, in his/her absence, the Company Secretary.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may determine any other period to be a Black-out Period from time to time (3.2(a)(v)). The policy does not state whether such additional periods are announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Use of Derivatives (which by definition includes options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars, and any transaction limiting economic risk) is banned outright over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Same outright ban extends to vested Company Securities still subject to a disposal restriction such as a Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unrestricted positions are expressly allowed, but remain a Dealing requiring the Designated Person's usual prior written approval under clause 5.1 and compliance with Black-out Periods.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: The Derivatives definition itself extends to 'any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities' - i.e. hedging - and use of Derivatives over unvested instruments is banned outright.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Hedging via a Derivative over vested, unrestricted securities is permitted subject to the standard prior written approval regime.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named; a structure limiting economic risk in any way over unvested securities is caught by the Derivatives definition and banned outright.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over vested unrestricted securities falls within the Derivatives definition and is permitted with standard prior approval.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Short selling as a technique is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named but would fall within 'any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities'; permitted over vested unrestricted securities with standard prior approval, banned over unvested or holding-locked securities under 6.2(a).
rules.evidence: Derivatives include ... any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on entering a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Company Securities - no vesting-state carve-out and no approval route exists.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities

rules.tier: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
rules.detail: Clause 6.3 is expressed to apply only to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on margin lending by non-Designated employees, consultants or contractors.
Absolute, unconditional ban on using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement - no vesting-state carve-out and no approval route exists.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: ... (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: The prohibition extends beyond margin loans strictly so-called to any 'similar funding arrangement' secured on Company Securities, which squarely catches a bank loan secured on the collared shares. No exemption, approval route or forced-sale carve-out is provided.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.detail: The policy contains no short-term or speculative dealing restriction.

In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).

exceptions.evidence: transfer Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board

exercise (but not Deal with the securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period

acquire (but not Deal with the securities following acquisition) Company shares by conversion of financial instruments giving rights to conversion to shares (eg. options or convertible securities) where the final date for the conversion of the security falls during a Black-out Period
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under a Company employee share plan
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Designated Person in an employee share plan where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee share scheme

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities

the Designated Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement

exemption_authority: The Chair (Approval Officer) may, acting with caution, grant a Disposal Consent to a Designated Person to dispose of or transfer (not acquire) Company Securities during a Black-out Period for severe financial hardship or a court order/legal requirement, subject to written application and supporting documentation, and only if the person has no Inside Information; the consent may carry conditions including its duration and the Board is notified of any consent granted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives include: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy's own definition of Derivatives expressly names 'collars', so a funded equity collar's put and call legs are squarely and expressly caught, not merely swept in by inference.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no clearance route, vesting-state carve-out, or exemption for this ban - the loan leg of a bank-funded collar cannot be implemented for any Designated Person, regardless of whether the shares are vested and unrestricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments ... Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar could in principle be executed over vested, unrestricted shares with standard clearance, even though the financing leg cannot be implemented at all - the two legs face fundamentally different treatment.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the Black-out Period override is limited to disposals/transfers for hardship or court order, so it could permit unwinding an existing collar position during a black-out but not entering into new derivative legs or a financing arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of a collar's derivative legs straddling the start of a Black-out Period is time-limited and cannot be adjusted once the black-out commences.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee, consultant or contractor (who is not a Designated Person) may, at any time, Deal in Company Securities if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Black-out Periods, the clause 5 approval regime, and the clause 6.3 margin loan ban are all expressed to apply only to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on secured financing by a non-Designated employee, though this is an unlikely profile for a bank collar counterparty.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any Designated Person: clause 6.3 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on entering a Margin Loan or 'similar funding arrangement' or using Company Securities as security for one, with no vesting-state carve-out, approval route or exemption authority. The derivative legs fare better - the Derivatives definition expressly names 'collars' as a captured instrument, and their use is banned outright only over unvested or holding-locked shares (6.2(a)); over vested, unrestricted shares, derivatives are expressly permitted (6.2(b)) subject to the standard prior written approval of the relevant Approving Officer, a 5 business day clearance validity, avoidance of Black-out Periods, and post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 5 business days. Because the financing leg is categorically prohibited with no clearance mechanism, a bank cannot lawfully take security over a Designated Person's Company Securities to fund the structure, even though the put and call could otherwise be cleared. The only partial relief is a narrow, Chair-approved Disposal Consent for disposals/transfers (not acquisitions or financing) during a Black-out Period in cases of genuine hardship or court order.
